messages:
mia: Heads-up — I just hit a weird divergence on the new quantized bring-up. After priming ~120k tokens the model output starts to drift mid-generation (tokens replaced with repeats/garbled seq). Repro steps below, minimal script and sample output. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: Which model + quant config? int8 or int4? GPU/kernel?

mia: redwood-opt-13b-q8 (quant8-v2), CUDA kernel v12.3, sequence chunking using our standard kvcache. Running on a single A100. Quick repro:
```python
from redwood import InferenceClient
c = InferenceClient(model="redwood-opt-13b-q8")
prefix = open('long_prompt.txt').read()  # ~120k tokens
resp = c.generate(prefix, max_tokens=512, stream=False)
print(resp.tokens[-80:])
```
Output starts fine, then around token 300 the tokens repeat and alignment shifts: 
```
... 'the', 'the', 'the', '\n', '4372', '4372', 'and', 'syst', 'syst'
```

priya: Sounds like a RoPE/position index wrap or kvcache index overflow. 120k crosses the 65536 boundary so if any index is stored in 16-bit or wrapped modulo behavior shows up. Did you see any off-by-one in the kvcache index math?

ethan: Also check whether the rotary scaling code path uses 32 vs 16-bit counters. We've seen drift when mixing int8 kernels with older rotary helpers. Can you paste the model shard/kernel version?

mia: Kernel metadata: kernel_hash=0x9f3a2c, build=2026-03-18, rotary_helper=rotary_v3. The kvcache uses a segmented index (uint32) but some helper offsets were cast to uint16 in the kernel patch for perf.

nina: Ran a quick smoke in CI with a truncated prompt to cross the 65536 boundary and saw kvcache index jump logged: 
```
[WARN] kv_index=65535 -> store_idx=0 (wrap) at 2026-03-19T22:12:04Z
[ERRO] mismatch detected, live seq!=prefill_seq
```
Latency/throughput looked normal until the corruption point.

ci-bot: automated-smoke: endpoint redwood-opt-13b-q8 on a100-1 — replicate=3/5 failures at step=generate(>64k). Logs attached (ci://runs/4221).

tomas: If it's a wrap, we can try two quick checks: 1) disable the uint16 cast (fallback to 32-bit counters) and retest; 2) toggle the rotary scaling fallback that applies a phase remap beyond 64k. Quick toggles: 
```
# runtime flags
--kvcache-index-width=32
--rotary-scale-mode=clamp
```
These are cheap to flip in the runtime and re-run the same smoke.

priya: Another angle: see if the quantized path uses a different priming stride. We've seen misaligned prefill stride + wrap cause the kv entries to map to wrong positions. Workaround is to re-prime in 32k chunks (overlap) or force a KV flush at boundaries.

sam: I'll schedule a small bisect: toggle the uint16 cast commit range (sha range: 7a1b..c3f5) and run 10 short reproduces crossing 65k and 131k. @nina can you run those on the a100-2? I can instrument the kvcache counters in the runtime to dump on WARN.

nina: Yep, I can run today. Will push a job that bangs the kernel with the --kvcache-index-width override and attach logs. ETA ~1.5h.

mia: Thanks — if it reproduces, let's pin as P0 for the bring-up and add a canary that stresses >64k. If it doesn't, we need to test alternate quant paths (int4) to see if it's a quant-specific interaction.

ethan: If you need a quick test case, use the attached mini-repro (I trimmed private text): long_prompt_small.json (1201 lines). Also add a golden-check of logits at token 250 and 310 to diff numeric deviation.

priya: Note: a plausible root cause is rotor-phase multiply being quantized differently between prefill and generation paths. Look for any separate codegen path for "prefill_rotor" vs "inflight_rotor".

mia: Assigned: sam + nina to run bisect & post logs to #eng-ml/artefacts. I'll add the failing sample to the repro folder and create a short dashboard to track reproductions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
